title: Liraglutide improves metabolic parameters and carotid intima‑media thickness in diabetic patients with the metabolic syndrome: an 18‑month prospective study

citation.title: Liraglutide improves metabolic parameters and carotid intima‑media thickness in diabetic patients with the metabolic syndrome: an 18‑month prospective study

what_it_measured.text: Fasting plasma samples for metabolic parameters were collected and carotid-intima media thickness (cIMT) was assessed by B-mode real-time ultrasound at baseline and every 6 months thereafter.
The primary endpoint of the present study was to investigate the effect of liraglutide on cardio-metabolic parameters.

dose.text: Liraglutide was added to metformin, at a dosage of 0.6 mg/day for 2 weeks, followed by a dose of 1.2 mg/day for the rest of the study.

endpoint.text: Secondary endpoints included the investigation of subclinical atherosclerosis, as assessed by cIMT, as well as the prevalence of the MetS during the 18-month follow-up.
The primary endpoint of the present study was to investigate the effect of liraglutide on cardio-metabolic parameters.

reported_results.text: Correlation analysis showed a significant association between changes in cIMT and triglycerides (r = 0.362; p < 0.0001).The MetS prevalence significantly reduced during the study, and the 26% of subjects no longer fulfilled the criteria for the MetS after 18 months.

Regarding plasma lipids, liraglutide therapy significantly decreased TC, TG and LDL-C (p = 0.0017, p = 0.0061 and p = 0.0039, respectively), while HDL-C increased, although the difference did not reach the statistical significance (p = 0.0853).
